metadata.purpose: Operational project memory for AI-agent-led development.
metadata.architecture: default single-process telegram bot/scraper/scheduler/delivery plus accepted opt-in BL-22 reliable Kafka roles, transactional scheduler/outbox, inbox-deduplicated rendering, leased Telegram delivery, content-free DLQ/recovery, stage-6 process/browser acceptance and stage-7 real Telegram acceptance; accepted BL-29 production shadow operations adds persistent role heartbeats and an authenticated bounded Kafka probe while reliable rollout remains off

entity.name: User
entity.summary: Telegram user identity, top-level preferences, and owner scope for per-user subscription limits.

entity.name: Subscription
entity.summary: Named digest configuration owned by one user, including editable AI filter and summary task prompts; can be created manually or from static global channel presets up to the configured per-user limit, and is shown in the subscription list with a next-digest countdown when enabled.

entity.name: SubscriptionChannel
entity.summary: Join entity between subscription and channel with subscribed_at baseline.

entity.name: DigestDelivery
entity.summary: Per-subscription processed-post record, delivered/skipped status, skip reason, summary metadata snapshot, and nullable reliable run/message provenance for backward-compatible old rows.

entity.name: DigestProcessingLog
entity.summary: Completed per-subscription processing-run totals for found, filtered, and included posts, including zero-result runs; reliable logs have a nullable unique run provenance while legacy rows remain valid.

entity.name: OnDemandDigest
entity.summary: Claimed or completed manual digest keyed by subscription, normalized period, and effective prompt fingerprint; persists rendered Telegram-safe messages for idempotent resend.

entity.name: ChatMessage
entity.summary: Persisted chat history for assistant context, visible system confirmations, and recent digest references.

entity.name: LlmUsage
entity.summary: Non-sensitive OpenRouter completion attempt telemetry: model, use case, status, available usage/cost fields, error class text, and timestamp without prompts or outputs.

entity.name: KnowledgeDocument
entity.summary: One fixed-schema semantic enrichment record for a canonical Post; synthetic metadata is not a citation source.

entity.name: KnowledgeRepresentation
entity.summary: Versioned summary, full, or original-text chunk retrieval representation linked to one parent Post.

entity.name: KnowledgeChannel, KnowledgeChannelRequest, KnowledgeImport, KnowledgeQuery, KnowledgeFeedback
entity.summary: Administrator-moderated public catalog with a hash-refreshed metadata-only description, temporary export audit trail with content-free enrichment/embedding/total cost totals, content-free per-stage search audit, and fixed-code feedback.

entity.name: OutboxEvent
entity.summary: Immutable content-free Kafka envelope and routing fields plus pending/publishing/published state, recoverable publication lease, durable attempts/backoff, broker acknowledgement metadata, and bounded machine-code error.

entity.name: InboxEvent, DigestRun, DigestOutboxMessage
entity.summary: Consumer/event dedup with recoverable leases, unique subscription/logical-slot runs, and ordered rendered Telegram-safe parts with durable attempts, retry timing, ambiguity and Telegram acknowledgement state. Subscription deletion cascades runs and their messages after existing delivery/log cleanup.

entity.name: DeadLetterRecord, DeadLetterReplay
entity.summary: UUID-keyed content-free terminal work generations and unreadable Kafka offsets plus append-only administrator replay audit with actor, time, result, generation and optional fixed outbox event.

entity.name: ReliabilityRoleHeartbeat
entity.summary: One latest content-free process generation per scheduler, outbox-relay, digest-worker, or telegram-delivery-worker, with starting/ready/stopped/failed lifecycle state, heartbeat and stop timestamps, and a bounded exception-class error code.

modules.module: Application bootstrap; role dispatch happens before app-only admin/bot/memory/knowledge imports, while the default app startup order remains unchanged and opt-in BL-22 roles run only under the separately enabled reliable-delivery policy.
Four fixed v1 content-free Kafka event contracts with checked-in JSON Schema/examples, deterministic serialization, sensitive-field rejection, byte limits, and compatibility checks.
aiokafka topic creation for missing topics only plus strict partition, replication, retention, cleanup, segment, and message-size drift checks.

Operator provisioning and opt-in role lifecycles with role-specific lazy imports, semantic readiness files bound to role, PID and process start ticks, plus best-effort PostgreSQL lifecycle heartbeats after dependency/producer/consumer startup. Only Telegram delivery receives BOT_TOKEN; roles do not run migrations or mount local Qdrant.

Content-free aiokafka admin/offset probe for broker latency, four fixed topic configurations and two fixed consumer groups/lags under one five-second deadline; active and cleanup tasks are single-flight, with safe ProbeTimeout/ProbeBusy/unavailable reports.
Caller-transaction enqueue, PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims including expired-lease recovery, stable envelope reconstruction, and owner-conditional publication/failure transitions.

enable_idempotence plus acks=all Kafka publication and a leased relay loop whose separate publication task has a hard timeout shorter than the lease even if client cancellation does not finish; timeout uses bounded full-jitter failure backoff and content-free transition logging/persistence without denying ambiguous broker acceptance.

Latest-due-slot transactional run producer, aiokafka manual-offset digest consumer, generic inbox/run lease recovery, renderer execution outside DB transactions with memory disabled, and atomic persistence of all ordered parts plus delivery outbox events before delivering state.
Generic consumer/event inbox dedup, unique scheduled run creation with root outbox enqueue, owner-conditional run leases, and atomic rendered-message/outcome/delivery-event persistence.

Generic manual-offset event consumer plus aiogram sender returning message IDs; claims persisted parts under recoverable leases, sends outside transactions with bounded timeout, classifies permanent/transient/ambiguous errors, and persists per-part outcomes and finalization.

Optional FastAPI/Uvicorn dashboard with PBKDF2 environment login, signed session, responsive Overview and Kafka tabs, read-only product/RAG/DLQ views, authenticated content-free role/broker/topic/group/lag and reliability queue/retry/lease gauges, and one CSRF/idempotency-protected single dead-letter replay command delegated outside AdminDashboardService.
Caller-transaction terminal upsert by work/generation, offset-keyed unreadable records, fixed v1 DLQ enqueue through OutboxRepository, and no raw event/message content or direct Kafka write.

Locks one dead-letter record, validates fixed run/message entities and states, appends one idempotent replay audit, and either creates exactly generation+1 root/delivery outbox work or records replay_rejected.

Unique-project PostgreSQL 16 and Kafka 3.9.2 process acceptance with clean migrations, stop/start semantic readiness matrix, production legacy-cycle exclusion, deterministic outage retry snapshot, guarded ACK/DB and DB/offset exits, immutable Kafka audits, delivery-only token scope, content-free metrics/transitions and fake Telegram fingerprints, real Chromium controls, and fail-hard exact-resource cleanup.

Accepted real Telegram E2E with production-app onboarding DB/log evidence, routing mirror, four isolated roles, delivery-only token secret, source/harness/image provenance, byte-audited republish and fail-hard cleanup. Successful report: .planning/evaluations/bl22-stage7/bl22-stage7-20260824T045339.868888Z.json.
Telegram command and callback routing, including subscription-list buttons with next-digest countdown labels and a subscription processing-log action for the last 24 hours.

User and subscription operations, product-limit enforcement for subscription/channel counts, plus bot-facing subscription label/list formatting with visible limit counters and user-scoped processing-log aggregates.
Channel page scraping orchestration, including bounded pagination to a requested period boundary.
Telegram page to ParsedPost conversion.

Due-checking, cascade batch summary filtering/synthesis, formatting, summary fallback, delivery/skipped persistence, completed processing-run logging including zero-result runs, and candidate-prompt rendering for isolated replay. The legacy scheduled loop skips subscriptions owned by the shared reliable-delivery policy.
Periodic scraping and LLM refresh plus a lightweight production legacy digest job entrypoint reusable by isolated ownership acceptance without importing the complete scheduler dependency graph.

OpenRouter chat, embeddings, bounded rerank, model-list, structured-output request parameters, HTTP error body previews, tool-probe adapter, and separately scheduled bounded content-free usage telemetry callback. The production API key has external PII-redaction and prompt-injection flag guardrails.

Minimal OpenAI-compatible async client for the direct DeepSeek API (deepseek-v4-flash), used only for bounded knowledge work (grounded RAG answers when the answer_direct_enabled flag is on, and the offline semantic claim judge). It records content-free usage telemetry (knowledge_answer_direct / knowledge_answer_judge) and never stores prompt or response content.

Content-free semantic claim judge for offline evaluation: DeepSeek-backed pairwise equivalence between a generated claim and a reviewed claim using only claim text and canonical post ids; returns True/False/None, aggregates verdicts only, and is versioned by a non-secret judge_version setting.

Hourly free-model refresh with persistent quality exclusions, DeepSeek V4 Flash paid emergency fallback, bounded assistant tool-support probing, in-memory runtime order, and per-use-case health backoff.
Channel persistence and lifecycle state.
Post upsert and retrieval.
Subscription and membership persistence.
Delivery dedup and summary metadata persistence, completed processing-run aggregate storage/querying, plus read-only subscription-period selection for prompt replay and on-demand rendering.
Atomic on-demand digest cache claim, completion, and retrieval.

LLM-first natural-language control orchestration over authorized tools, plus a deterministic public-RAG router that uses a fresh trusted catalog snapshot, never silently widens catalog scope, and bypasses mem0 for catalog-routing/search turns.
Internal MCP-like product tools scoped to the current Telegram user, including read-only digest prompt replay, processing-log aggregates, and idempotent on-demand digest generation.

Cron validation, 15-minute minimum interval enforcement, stable latest elapsed slot calculation with latest-only catch-up for cron/legacy timezone schedules, due checks, next-digest timestamps, and safe localized labels.
Independent mem0-backed semantic memory layer around assistant turns; local Qdrant/history files live under .data/mem0.
Shared Telegram HTML instructions and sanitizer for assistant replies and digest text.

Authorized catalog moderation, durable canonical-post import, hash-refreshed metadata-only descriptions, fixed-schema enrichment, bounded retries, parent-scoped hybrid retrieval, structured claim answers with inline canonical citations, and reranking with provider/cost fallback. When answer_direct_enabled is set, interactive grounded answers run through the direct DeepSeek API (deepseek-v4-flash) instead of OpenRouter, with the OpenRouter chain retained as fallback. Matching graph/vector, code-navigation, and documentation questions receive small fixed retrieval facets before parent fusion; their selected facet sources are mandatory citations in the structured answer contract. The grounded-answer contract accepts an honest model self-assessed refusal (empty claims plus evidence_sufficient false) as a valid terminal answer and renders the localized insufficient-material notice, while provider/transport failure keeps the source-backed fallback claim. The candidate applies to allowlisted canary IDs or, with the global all-users flag plus the rollout master switch, to every user. It commits a content-free retrieval trace before the interactive answer call, and stage/provider/total timeouts bound the turn while stage timings are always recorded. The offline evaluator can atomically checkpoint only numeric aggregates and resume one exact dataset/configuration after a provider interruption.

Offline labelled-dataset evaluation with dev/eval split filtering, negative-case abstention/false-attribution metrics measured by the generated answer (empty vs non-empty claims) rather than raw retrieval emptiness, source sufficiency plus claim-coverage sufficiency, citation precision/recall/F1 and thesis-to-link placement, deterministic claim heuristics and an optional content-free DeepSeek semantic claim judge, content-free atomic checkpoints, and operator flags --split, --judge, --print-samples, --limit, --checkpoint, --rerank-limit, --direct, --concurrency. The case loop is parallelized with a bounded semaphore (concurrency up to 10); each case uses its own isolated session and external provider calls (embed/rerank/answer/judge) are concurrent-safe, while Qdrant client initialization is guarded by a thread lock.

Content-free DeepSeek semantic claim judge plus operator-only calibration tooling: the judge compares a generated claim against a reviewed claim by coverage of essential aspects (central assertion plus negations, limitations, scope, mappings) and is calibrated against a fixed operator-labelled pair set (v6 prompt, agreement 17/19 = 0.895); judge_prompt_score scores a prompt against a fixed labelled file without regenerating answers.
Paragraph-aware representations, isolated local Qdrant vector access, parent collapse/RRF, context reconstruction, and original Telegram permalink rendering.
Chat history persistence and recent digest retrieval.

Docker runtime starts PostgreSQL and the app by default; opt-in profile bl22 adds one internal KRaft broker and four continuously restartable roles. BL-29 shadow observation requires explicit app KAFKA_ENABLED=1 with RELIABLE_DIGEST_ENABLED=0 and MEMORY_ENABLED=1; only the default app runs migrations/mounts .data and legacy remains sole delivery. Profile-off keeps the app Kafka setting disabled.

flow.name: User onboarding and preferences
flow.summary: Registers user, shows an editable Telegram-safe HTML /start guide without a duplicated external title, positions Channel Scanner as an AI service for selected public text Telegram channels, focus management, flexible filtering, scheduled digests, and future knowledge-base use, picks language, stores timezone and language, and can run in one allowlisted E2E chat for black-box verification.

flow.name: Subscription management
flow.summary: Create manually or from static global channel presets up to the configured per-user subscription limit, rename, configure, enable, disable, and delete named subscriptions; the subscription list shows enabled subscriptions with a short next-digest countdown and visible subscription/channel limit counters, while each subscription exposes found/filtered/included processing totals for the last 24 hours. Deletion first removes delivery/processing/manual/channel state, then database cascades reliable runs/messages while dead-letter and replay audit history survives with nullable entity links.

flow.name: Channel membership management
flow.summary: Validates public usernames, adds shared channels manually or from presets up to the configured per-subscription channel limit, removes channel membership per subscription.

flow.name: Scheduled scraping
flow.summary: Iterates active channels, fetches pages, parses posts, stores new posts, marks channel state.

flow.name: Scheduled digest delivery
flow.summary: Selects due subscriptions, finds unprocessed posts, renders digests, sends Telegram messages, stores delivered and skipped processing state, and persists found/filtered/included processing totals after each completed run, including zero-result runs.

flow.name: On-demand digest delivery
flow.summary: Resolves a user-owned named subscription and a timezone-aware period, claims an idempotent cache key, paginates its channels to the interval start while retaining at most 100 matching posts per channel, stores posts idempotently, renders and sends normal digest messages as the turn's only visible output, and caches them for exact resend without changing DigestDelivery, DigestProcessingLog, or last_digest_at.

flow.name: LLM summary generation
flow.summary: Uses an hourly refreshed OpenRouter free-model pool, excluding permanently disqualified models, followed by DeepSeek V4 Flash as a paid emergency fallback for empty-post pre-skip plus structured JSON schema filter-then-synthesize batch summaries. The production OpenRouter API key externally redacts configured PII and flags prompt-injection matches; it does not apply thematic political/crime moderation. The flow supports editable task-only AI filter prompts while app-owned memory/preference handling remains mandatory, supports editable summary prompts with an approved brief default, exposes candidate prompt overrides for read-only replay, enforces target-language/plain-field prompt rules, strips accidental leading topic bullets before rendering source-linked topic bullets, retries the next model on invalid JSON, and falls back safely to 200-character mode on failure or empty model output.

flow.name: Natural-language bot control
flow.summary: Uses an hourly refreshed OpenRouter free-model assistant pool with DeepSeek V4 Flash as the paid emergency fallback and cached tool-support probes, stops inline probing once a confirmed assistant model is available, and uses internal tools to inspect and mutate bot product state including AI filter/summary prompts and read-only processing-log aggregates; for dissatisfaction with digest output, it first asks for a missing desired result, then prioritizes replaying a persisted subscription period through candidate prompts without sending or persisting state before proposing or mutating prompts. Explicit confirmation remains required before prompt mutation. The assistant prompt includes current product limits and tool executions are capped per turn; explains capabilities/how-to-use questions in simple language, shows Telegram typing feedback while the turn runs, then emits deterministic localized Telegram-safe HTML confirmations with bold subscription names.

flow.name: Assistant semantic memory
flow.summary: Retrieves and updates mem0 semantic memories independently from the assistant; memory mutation tools are not exposed to the model. Compose mounts ./.data to /app/.data so local Qdrant/history state survives app recreates. The app creates one shared process-local memory service for scheduler digest filtering and bot assistant turns.

flow.name: Read-only product dashboard with one narrow recovery command
flow.entrypoints: HTTPS csd.ai-research.arha.digital through Caddy; internal FastAPI server
flow.summary: Uses an environment-configured PBKDF2 password hash and signed session to show existing responsive product/RAG aggregates plus content-free DLQ list/detail. Product state remains read-only except for the sole CSRF/idempotency-protected append-only recovery command for one fixed dead-letter run/message; no arbitrary event, bulk replay, discard, prompts, posts, messages, answers, or provider content are exposed.

flow.name: Public-channel knowledge search
flow.summary: The assistant loads READY catalog names, metadata-only descriptions, counts, and sync timestamps as trusted context. It lists that snapshot without a tool round; explicit @username searches one channel, while channel-free questions propose one confirmed match or a choice of up to three and never widen scope silently. RAG routing/search bypasses mem0. Grounded answers contain validated structured claims with inline one-to-five original Telegram links; descriptions and retrieval representations are not evidence. Matching fixed retrieval facets require their selected sources to be cited. The candidate applies to allowlisted canary IDs or, with the global all-users flag plus the rollout master switch, to every user; it reranks the maximum 20 scope-authorized parents, and interactive stage/provider/total timeouts bound the turn while stage timings are always recorded.

flow.name: Knowledge catalog moderation and import
flow.entrypoints: Assistant requestKnowledgeChannel tool, Telegram administrator callbacks and JSON document upload
flow.summary: Users create pending public-channel requests. Only configured Telegram administrators approve/reject and upload bounded official JSON exports; imports persist canonical posts before optional enrichment/indexing. Failed enrichment or vectorization retains bounded retry/error state for the four-hour job, and raw export JSON is never stored in PostgreSQL.

flow.name: BL-22 Kafka stage-1 bootstrap
flow.entrypoints: docker compose --profile bl22, src.reliability.cli, explicit src.main --role arguments
flow.summary: Creates four fixed v1 topics on one internal KRaft broker, fails on topic drift, and runs safe role processes that prove dependency readiness and persist lifecycle heartbeats while all business processing remains in the unchanged default app path when reliable delivery is disabled.

flow.name: BL-29 Kafka shadow role lifecycle and authenticated operations tab
flow.entrypoints: explicit KAFKA_ENABLED=1 plus docker compose --profile bl22; GET /admin/api/kafka/operations; Kafka tab in /admin
flow.summary: With RELIABLE_DIGEST_ENABLED=0 and MEMORY_ENABLED=1, Kafka and all four roles stay up in shadow mode while legacy is the sole delivery path. Roles persist best-effort process-generation lifecycle heartbeats. The authenticated Kafka tab loads only when opened, refreshes every 15 seconds while active, and combines a bounded single-flight broker/topic/group/lag probe with PostgreSQL heartbeat freshness, outbox/retry/expired-lease/DLQ gauges and up to 20 recent safe machine-code errors. Missing shadow consumer groups are expected inactive; broker failure is unavailable and does not break Overview. Production Compose smoke was accepted on 2026-08-24 after migration 0025 with drift-free broker/topics, four ready heartbeats below 10 seconds, HTTP 200, zero reliable work/errors, and healthy legacy app/mem0/admin.

flow.name: BL-22 Kafka stage-2 shadow outbox relay
flow.summary: Claims caller-enqueued content-free events under recoverable PostgreSQL leases, bounds each idempotent all-acks Kafka publication wait before lease expiry, and conditionally stores broker metadata or bounded retry state. A timeout is ambiguous and may lead to duplicate publication of the same immutable event. With reliable delivery disabled it remains shadow-only; stage 3 can explicitly enqueue scheduler/render events.

flow.name: BL-22 reliable digest scheduling and durable rendering
flow.summary: For explicitly policy-owned subscriptions, creates one run/root event for only the latest elapsed schedule slot, relays and consumes it with manual offsets, recovers inbox/run leases, renders once outside the transaction with no memory service, and atomically saves every ordered part/outcome/delivery event before moving the run to delivering. Telegram delivery is not implemented.

flow.name: BL-22 persistent Telegram part delivery and run finalization
flow.summary: The fixed telegram-delivery-v1 group validates delivery events, inbox-deduplicates them, claims one due or stale persisted part with SKIP LOCKED, and calls Telegram outside a transaction under a send timeout shorter than its lease. Durable success stores only that part's delivery/chat provenance; the last sent part finalizes one processing log and last_digest_at. A transient result stores retry work; stage 5 extends terminal outcomes with atomic content-free DB and DLQ outbox state.

flow.name: BL-22 content-free dead letters and single recovery
flow.entrypoints: terminal digest/Telegram transactions, Kafka contract rejection callbacks, POST /admin/api/dead-letters/{id}/replay
flow.summary: Terminal work and identifiable invalid envelopes atomically persist one dead-letter generation and fixed v1 DLQ OutboxEvent. Unreadable payloads persist only topic/partition/offset and commit without a Kafka DLQ event. One authenticated command locks and validates a run/message, then appends exactly one next-generation work event or replay_rejected audit.

flow.name: BL-22 isolated full process and browser acceptance
flow.summary: Builds the current image in a unique Compose project, migrates clean PostgreSQL 16, provisions Kafka 3.9.2, and starts scheduler/relay/render/delivery separately. It proves process-generation readiness, legacy exclusion, outage/crash recovery, immutable republish, stale leases, fake-Telegram ambiguity, partial restart, DLQ, token scope, transitions and browser replay. Stage 6 itself did not prove real Telegram; that remaining acceptance was subsequently completed by stage 7 on 2026-08-24.

flow.name: BL-22 accepted isolated real Telegram delivery and duplicate suppression
flow.summary: Accepted on 2026-08-24 by real Telegram E2E report .planning/evaluations/bl22-stage7/bl22-stage7-20260824T045339.868888Z.json. One send was accepted; run, root inbox and delivery inbox completed; one part sent; exact duplicate was suppressed; production app remained continuous; routing identity mirroring and fail-hard cleanup succeeded. Total duration was 450.883s. This closes BL-22 but does not enable general rollout: default reliable remains off and legacy remains active.

invariant.name: No duplicate delivery per subscription/post
invariant.summary: The same post must not be delivered or skipped twice for the same subscription; any DigestDelivery status removes it from pending selection.

invariant.name: No duplicate persisted post per channel/post_id
invariant.summary: Re-scraping must be idempotent for existing Telegram posts.

invariant.name: No historical posts before subscribed_at
invariant.summary: Posts published before a subscription added the channel must not appear in future digests for that subscription.

invariant.name: Timezone and frequency control due delivery
invariant.summary: Daily and hourly digests plus subscription-list countdown labels must respect user timezone, notification cron, and legacy subscription frequency fallback.

invariant.name: Summary failures must not block delivery
invariant.summary: If free summary model refresh, structured filter/synthesis JSON, model calls, empty model output, or model health selection fail, the bot must retry usable models including the final DeepSeek V4 Flash paid emergency fallback when possible and still send a short digest for non-empty posts using normal digest grouping; empty extracted posts are skipped before LLM calls.

invariant.name: Reply context never replaces current post body
invariant.summary: Scraped reply posts must store and summarize the current post text, excluding replied-to/quoted Telegram context from digest rendering and LLM input.

invariant.name: Visible bot output must remain Telegram-safe HTML
invariant.summary: Rendered digest and assistant output must keep allowed tags and valid links without raw Markdown or broken Telegram formatting; batch topic summaries are rendered with one app-owned bullet marker even if a model returns a leading bullet; assistant mutation confirmations must localize RU/EN text and bold subscription names with escaped Telegram HTML.

invariant.name: Channel membership is per subscription, not global per user
invariant.summary: Each named subscription has its own channel list and delivery scope.

invariant.name: Notification cron interval is bounded
invariant.summary: Assistant-provided notification cron expressions must not fire more often than every 15 minutes; valid interval schedules such as every 3 hours must render in tools and bot screens without crashing.

invariant.name: Assistant mutations go through authorized tools
invariant.summary: The assistant can mutate product state only through user-scoped product tools, never raw repositories or database sessions; assistant model selection must prefer models with confirmed tool support.

invariant.name: Assistant memory is not tool-managed by the model
invariant.summary: mem0 memory retrieval/extraction is performed by an independent layer; the assistant does not receive save/delete memory tools.

invariant.name: Local mem0 state persists outside the container
invariant.summary: When local mem0 storage is enabled, Qdrant and history files must stay under the host-mounted .data path, be excluded from git and Docker build context, and be accessed by only one process-local memory service to avoid Qdrant local lock conflicts.

invariant.name: Editable filter prompts cannot override app guardrails
invariant.summary: User-editable AI filter prompts are limited to the filter Task. JSON schema output, dynamic post serialization, and explicit memory/preference handling are app-owned prompt sections outside editable text.

invariant.name: Product limits are enforced at mutation boundaries
invariant.summary: Configured limits cap assistant tool executions per turn, subscriptions per user, and channels per subscription for both UI and natural-language assistant mutation paths; visible subscription lists and assistant instructions expose those limits to users/LLM.

invariant.name: Prompt replay is isolated from delivery state
invariant.summary: Prompt replay may read persisted posts within a user-owned subscription, its channel subscribed_at baseline, and a selected interval, but must not scrape, send Telegram messages, create DigestDelivery or ChatMessage rows, or update last_digest_at.

invariant.name: Processing logs are completed and user-scoped
invariant.summary: Only a successful completed subscription run may persist found/filtered/included totals, including zero-result runs; menu and assistant reads must stay within the current user's subscription and never mutate delivery state.

invariant.name: On-demand digest is cached and isolated
invariant.summary: The same user-owned subscription, normalized [start, end) period, and effective filter/summary prompts must reuse one rendered result without repeating scraping or LLM generation; manual delivery must not create scheduled delivery or processing-log state or update last_digest_at, and no assistant reply may repeat or summarize tool-rendered digest text in the same turn.

invariant.name: Admin product state is read-only except append-only dead-letter recovery
invariant.summary: Dashboard routes require configured password-hash login and signed session. Existing product/RAG views cannot mutate state; the sole mutation requires CSRF plus Idempotency-Key and can only replay one stored run/message into one next-generation fixed outbox event or append a rejection audit.

invariant.name: LLM telemetry is non-blocking and content-free
invariant.summary: Telemetry stores only model, use case, status, available tokens/cost, error class text, and timestamp. It is scheduled separately with a bounded write attempt; its delay or failure must not hold up normal model fallback, digest delivery, or assistant turns.

invariant.name: External OpenRouter input guardrails have a narrow scope
invariant.summary: The production API key redacts configured PII before provider forwarding and records prompt-injection matches in flag mode. It does not block political, criminal, or true-crime subject matter, does not scan model output, and must not be switched to block mode until the client treats a guardrail 403 as terminal.

invariant.name: Kafka event contracts are content-free and bounded
invariant.summary: Only supported v1 identifiers and routing metadata can serialize; post/message text, HTML, prompts, tokens, secrets, provider responses, unknown fields, invalid versions, and oversized events are rejected before publication.

invariant.name: Kafka stage-1 roles cannot process business work
invariant.summary: The opt-in roles run with RUN_MIGRATIONS=0, no .data mount, and no Caddy network. Under default reliable-delivery settings scheduler/digest/Telegram roles remain readiness-only and outbox relay is shadow-only; explicit stage-3 rollout activates only scheduler/rendering, never Telegram sending.

invariant.name: Outbox enqueue is atomic and publication is recoverable
invariant.summary: Enqueue never commits the caller session; due or expired publishing rows are claimed with PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, transitions require the current lease owner, and each separate publication task has a hard configured deadline shorter than the lease even if client cancellation resists completion. A timeout or lost acknowledgement is ambiguous and can cause the same event_id, key, and contract bytes to be republished. Persisted errors are bounded content-free codes.

invariant.name: Legacy and reliable scheduled paths never own the same subscription
invariant.summary: A disabled-by-default master plus allowlist/all-subscriptions policy is shared by reliable scheduler and legacy DigestService. A production legacy scheduler cycle must skip a due reliable-owned subscription before sender invocation or legacy delivery persistence. All-subscriptions rollout is refused while mem0 is enabled; reliable rendering always receives memory_service=None.

invariant.name: Completed root events never rerender
invariant.summary: Consumer/event and subscription/slot uniqueness plus recoverable inbox/run leases ensure duplicates after a completed database outcome commit their Kafka offset without rebuilding messages. Every part and delivery event is persisted in one transaction before the run becomes delivering.

invariant.name: Reliable Telegram attempts are durable and part-scoped
invariant.summary: Only the Telegram delivery role receives BOT_TOKEN. Every send attempt is incremented before the external call, send timeout is shorter than the recoverable lease, 429 Retry-After is a minimum over capped full jitter, timeout/network/stale sends are marked ambiguous, and a sent part is never claimed again.

invariant.name: Reliable runs finalize once after durable part outcomes
invariant.summary: Each acknowledged part atomically persists only its DigestDelivery and ChatMessage provenance. Exactly the final sent part creates the unique run processing log, updates last_digest_at and completed_at; empty runs do the same with zero totals and no delivery event.

invariant.name: Terminal work and recovery remain atomic, content-free and idempotent
invariant.summary: A terminal work generation has one DB dead letter and one v1 DLQ OutboxEvent in the same transaction; there is no direct Kafka write. Unreadable offsets have no DLQ event without contract IDs. One row-locked replay key appends at most one generation and outbox event, while missing entities append replay_rejected without work. Deleting a subscription cascades its run/messages but preserves dead-letter/audit identity through SET NULL links and immutable entity_ref/correlation.

invariant.name: A clean PostgreSQL database migrates to head in one run
invariant.summary: Before Alembic runs revisions, ensure_version_table_capacity creates or expands alembic_version.version_num to VARCHAR(64), so descriptive revision IDs work on both absent and existing version tables. Stage 6 makes upgrade-to-head the first operation on every fresh PostgreSQL volume.

invariant.name: Real Telegram acceptance cannot overlap or escape its isolated scope
invariant.summary: Stage 7 preserves exact production app generation, mirrors only tester routing identity, scopes the token secret to delivery, suppresses exact root duplicates and removes all isolated resources before evidence is accepted. The successful 2026-08-24 report proves these conditions with accepted_send_count=1 and completed states. This invariant is accepted for BL-22 while global reliable rollout remains disabled and legacy ownership remains default.

invariant.name: Kafka shadow mode never takes delivery ownership
invariant.summary: BL-29 operations require explicit KAFKA_ENABLED=1 with RELIABLE_DIGEST_ENABLED=0 and MEMORY_ENABLED=1. The app keeps mem0 active, no subscription is reliable-owned, scheduler/digest/delivery roles stay readiness-only, reliable-disabled domain flows enqueue no new work, and legacy scheduled delivery remains the sole user path. Production Compose smoke accepted this boundary on 2026-08-24 with zero new reliable DigestRun.

invariant.name: Stopped, failed, stale and current role generations remain distinct
invariant.summary: Each expected role owns one latest generation row. Initial replacement is atomic and older/different generations cannot overwrite the winner with later periodic updates. Heartbeats are best-effort with bounded writes and cannot stop business work. A non-terminal heartbeat older than 30 seconds is stale; stopped and failed lifecycle states take precedence and are never healthy.

invariant.name: Kafka operations telemetry is content-free
invariant.summary: The authenticated snapshot exposes only rollout/memory booleans, fixed topic/group names and metadata, lag, role generation/lifecycle/ages, queue counts/ages, technical entity identifiers and bounded safe error codes. It excludes event payloads, posts, digest text/HTML, prompts, chat content/IDs, tokens, subscription allowlist values, exception messages and raw logs.

invariant.name: Kafka operations probing is bounded and single-flight
invariant.summary: One probe owns a hard five-second deadline. Timeout or broker/API failure maps to a safe unavailable report; while an active probe or cancellation-resistant admin/consumer cleanup remains, automatic and manual refreshes create no second client and return ProbeBusy. Kafka failure does not invalidate the separately loaded Overview.

invariant.name: Knowledge citations are canonical parent posts
invariant.summary: Post.content is stored once as the source of truth. Summary cards, full embeddings, chunks, vector payloads, and LLM outputs can retrieve or rank but never become user-visible citations.

invariant.name: Public catalog discovery resolves one explicit safe scope
invariant.summary: A channel-free question may rank metadata-only READY catalog entries, but cannot search posts until the user confirms a clear match or chooses one channel. The catalog snapshot, descriptions, memories, and chat history are never answer evidence.

invariant.name: Knowledge scope and baseline apply before parent sources
invariant.summary: Subscription search enforces owner, linked channels, and subscribed_at on parent Post records before lexical/vector candidates can become sources; catalog history requires an explicit catalog-channel scope.

invariant.name: Knowledge fallback and Qdrant isolation
invariant.summary: Knowledge enrichment, catalog descriptions, and grounded interactive answers call their configured direct DeepSeek V4 Flash model and record content-free telemetry. Failed enrichment and vectorization retain bounded attempts plus content-free errors for later automatic retry; exhausted failures preserve normal lexical search. The one process-local knowledge Qdrant client uses .data/knowledge/qdrant and never shares mem0's path or collection.

invariant.name: Knowledge imports never create a digest backlog
invariant.summary: Every post from an administrator JSON catalog backfill receives a subscription-scoped skipped delivery record with reason knowledge_import_backfill for existing channel memberships. This keeps canonical/RAG persistence separate from normal scraper-driven digest eligibility.

invariant.name: Candidate RAG is reversibly gated and safe
invariant.summary: The BL-21 candidate is off by default for arbitrary deployments and is selected only when the rollout master switch is on and either the explicit Telegram allowlist matches or the global all-users flag is set. This production configuration permanently selects the dedicated E2E tester bot and, after an operator decision, every user through the global flag. It may send at most 20 scope-authorized canonical public posts to the reranker; missing credentials, provider errors, invalid results, unavailable cost, or configured cost-cap retain baseline ranking. Interactive stage/provider/total timeouts bound the turn while stage timings remain recorded.

invariant.name: RAG rollout evidence is content-free
invariant.summary: RAG configuration snapshots, query telemetry, evaluation records, API payloads, and dashboard views contain identifiers and aggregate metrics only; they must not expose user IDs, allowlists, raw questions, posts, answers, or prompt text.
